item.title: Ohio school district's fiscal crisis follows state-level changes
item.description: Hamilton City Schools blames state funding formula changes and property tax reforms for a fiscal emergency that has prompted school closures and deep cuts.

item.title: GFOA: MSRB appears to make issuers feel regulated rather than protected
item.description: MSRB CEO Mark Kim described GFOA's letter suggesting changes the MSRB could make as "very constructive, very valuable."

item.title: Demographics drive downgrades for three Northeast universities
item.description: Downgrades of three private universities in the Northeast reflect enrollment pressures facing the higher education sector, particularly in that region.

item.title: Corpus Christi takes action to increase water supply
item.description: The Texas city, which is a regional water supplier, is turning to several sources to boost dwindling water supplies amid an ongoing drought.

item.title: Reconciliation could pose threat to tax exemption
item.description: Public finance advocates are trying to interpret mixed signals about plans to pass a major reconciliation bill that could put the threat to the tax-exempt status of munis back on the table.

item.title: Lawmakers agree on need for permitting reform, but Trump's role hampers progress
item.description: Democrats said they've paused negotiations until the administration relaxes its anti-clean energy stance.

item.title: Dallas transit agency member city exodus threat grows
item.description: Addison is the sixth of Dallas Area Rapid Transit's 13 member cities where voters will decide in May whether to drop out of the agency.

item.title: Trump administration may grind Gateway tunnels to a halt
item.description: The rail tunnel connecting New York and New Jersey is well underway, but the project can't continue without federal funds the adminstration has choked off.

item.title: Munis, USTs little changed after FOMC holds rates
item.description: "Markets are reading this as a strategic pause, not a policy shift," said Gina Bolvin, president of Bolvin Wealth Management Group.

item.title: Dearborn Public Schools mulls up to $1.5B of bonds
item.description: After voters rejected a 2019 bond proposal, Michigan's Dearborn Public Schools is mulling a possible $500 million, $1 billion or $1.5 billion bond this year.
